articles.summary: Kendall Rae Johnson is 10 years old and reportedly the youngest certified farmer in the United States.
articles.body: Kendall Rae Johnson is 10 years old and reportedly the youngest certified farmer in the United States. The report, written by Chris Welch in Atlanta, says she began farming at the age of three and started her business at six. On any given day, she might be giving a tour to local schoolchildren, selling her produce from her front yard or at farmers' markets around the Atlanta area, or sitting behind a table signing autographs for her children's book about farming. The outlet also reports that she has now been gifted a total of 40 acres towards her ultimate goal of having 100 acres on which to farm and raise cattle.How did America’s youngest certified farmer start farming at age 3In an interview with Spectrum News, Kendall dates the start of her farming to a very young age. 'I started farming at the age of 3,' she told the outlet. The report says her passion can be traced back to her great-grandmother, who taught her how to grow collard greens when she was just a toddler.Kendall described that first experience to Spectrum News. 'I thought it was magical to me, so I pretty much started my farming journey from there,' she said. 'It just felt magical that something so small turned into something so big.' According to the report, her mother, Ursula Johnson, said it is a passion her daughter was born with. 'This is organically out of her,' Johnson said. 'Mom and dad — we are just following in the footsteps of a child.'How did Kendall launch her farming business at age 6Kendall's farming grew into a business at an early age. 'And I started my business at the age of 6,' she told the outlet. The report describes her as the youngest certified farmer in the United States.Her days involve several different activities. She could be giving a tour to local school kids, selling her produce from her front yard or at farmers' markets around the Atlanta area, or signing autographs at a table for her children's book about farming. According to the report, this is a step towards her ultimate goal of having 100 acres of land on which to farm and raise cattle.The report adds that her efforts have been recognised by South Carolina State University, which has offered her a full-ride scholarship. College is still years away. Ursula Johnson told the outlet, 'She's gonna do something, and I guarantee you it's gonna be fabulous.'How does Kendall want to teach more people to farmKendall wants to share what she knows. 'I like farming, and I want to teach more people how to farm like me,' she said. The report defines food deserts as areas of the country and the world that are often low-income and have limited access to fresh food. Kendall told the outlet that the problem could be fixed 'by just teaching people how to grow their own food.' Spectrum News also quotes Kendall on what farming means to her. articles.body:
Brazil is set to face India in a historic international friendly on Saturday at the Vivekananda Yuba Bharati Krirangan in Kolkata.

India vs Brazil – Match preview and team news

Venue: Vivekananda Yuba Bharati Krirangan, Kolkata

Head coach Khalid Jamil has a fully fit squad at his disposal as the Blue Tigers prepare for this historic clash following a resilient draw against Panama.

Veteran captain and goalkeeper Gurpreet Singh Sandhu is set to win his landmark 90th international cap and faces a challenging evening against world-class opposition.

In-form forward Ryan Williams, who found the net against Panama, is expected to spearhead the Indian attack alongside Manvir Singh.

The defensive line will rely heavily on the partnership of Anwar Ali and Bijoy Varghese to absorb the intense pressure. Jamil is anticipated to deploy a disciplined 4-4-2 formation, emphasising a low defensive block and structured counter-attacks.

Midfielders Apuia and Ricky John Shabong will play a critical role in disrupting transitions and shielding the backline in front of a passionate home crowd.

Head coach Carlo Ancelotti will be without Barcelona winger Raphinha, who withdrew from the 26-member experimental squad due to a right-thigh injury.

He joins Chelsea's Joao Pedro and Roma's Wesley on the sidelines, with no replacement called up. Despite these absences, the Seleção boasts a star-studded lineup headlined by Real Madrid talisman Vinicius Junior alongside teenage sensations Endrick and Estevao Willian.

Experienced defenders Marquinhos and Gabriel Magalhaes will anchor the backline, while Bruno Guimaraes controls the midfield tempo.

Fluminense's Gabriel Martinelli has also joined the squad as a late addition. Ancelotti is expected to field an aggressive 4-3-3 system designed to dominate possession and exploit the wings. The heavy favourites look to utilise their technical superiority and high-pressing style to break down India's defence early in the match.

India enters the historic match searching for consistency, showing a form guide of W-L-L-L-D-D in their last six fixtures. After a 2–1 victory against Hong Kong in Asian Cup qualifying, the Blue Tigers suffered three straight friendly defeats to Jamaica (0–2), Zimbabwe (0–1), and Tajikistan (1–3). However, they have shown defensive resilience recently, grinding out consecutive 1–1 draws in their last two matches against Tajikistan and Panama.

Brazil comes into this friendly in formidable shape, carrying a strong form guide of L-W-W-W-D-W over their last six matches. Following a round-of-16 exit against Norway at the 2026 World Cup, the Seleção bounced back under Carlo Ancelotti. In their most recent international break, Brazil remained undefeated against Australia, playing out a tight 1–1 draw in the first leg before securing a dominant 4–2 victory in the second.

India: Singh Sandhu; A Singh, Varghese, Ali, Mishra; Apuia, Thapa; Partap Singh, Williams, Kuruniyan; M Singh

Brazil: Souza; Matheuzinho, Marquinhos, Gabriel, D Santos; A Santos, Martinelli, Guimares; Estevao, Vinicius, Endrick
